data.title: Generate a readable city block from parcels
data.summary: A 60 by 40 m block, six parcel rectangles and street setback of 3 m. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: Geometry Nodes provides procedural geometry, instances and field-based controls.

prerequisites: An authorized Blender Geometry Nodes environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: A 60 by 40 m block, six parcel rectangles and street setback of 3 m.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent city block workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: A 60 by 40 m block, six parcel rectangles and street setback of 3 m. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Convert parcel outlines into building footprints after applying the setback
Extrude height from a small explicit table instead of random uncontrolled towers
Keep roads and pedestrian routes separate; inspect intersections from street level

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned generate a readable city block from parcels candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: All buildings remain within their parcels
Every entry has a route to a public street
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: Procedural massing is not zoning compliance or structural design.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: Use semantic IDs for parcels so regeneration preserves annotations.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me generate a readable city block from parcels in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: A 60 by 40 m block, six parcel rectangles and street setback of 3 m. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: All buildings remain within their parcels; Every entry has a route to a public street. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
